snippet.title: Is it possible to transplant organs from animals to humans?
snippet.description:
I got literal goosebumps researching this topic! Living with a pig's heart sounds like pure science fiction, but it is rapidly becoming our reality. I dug deep into the wild world of xenotransplantation, where scientists are altering pig genetics so our bodies won't reject their organs. We are already seeing heart and kidney transplants, and I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw a human ear grown on a mouse! The full success rates are still climbing, but if things keep moving this fast, traditional organ donation might disappear entirely. It really makes me question the ethics of turning animals into spare part factories, but the potential to save millions of human lives is massive. What side are you on? Drop a comment below and let me know!

snippet.title: Can We Read Memories From A Dead Brain?
snippet.description:
When they entered the brains of the dead and watched their memories in the TV show Fringe, I was really excited watching it. But is this actually possible in real life? In this video, I compared legendary science fiction with scientific reality. What I learned during my research genuinely surprised me! I think it's so weird that, except for the first few critical minutes after death, no memories can be extracted like a USB flash drive because the brain's organic structure degrades rapidly. Honestly, knowing that the human brain doesn't work like a computer hard drive creeped me out a bit. What do you think about digital immortality? Would you want to save your memories on a chip? Now, on our previous trips to East Asia, we definitely noticed the prevalence of 7-Elevens pretty much everywhere - and not only were we surprised by how widespread and popular they were - we quickly realized, they had a lot of pretty awesome stuff we don’t have in the states - like, baos, teas, sandos, noodles, iced coffees, unique chip flavors, pancake sandwiches, corn ice cream - and more!! And once we returned - I started to notice how many people online were also going to international 7-Elevens and doing snack hauls - and I realized - this is a convenience store movement!! 

So on our travels over the past year, we’ve collected 7-Eleven tours and hauls in each country we visited - Singapore, Malaysia, and Japan… to try out some viral snacks, and generally compare them, but also mostly just to feast! Which country’s 7-Eleven should we visit next?
